chapters.title: David at Nob and Gath
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 21

The Holy Bread

1David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech came trembling to meet David and said to him, "Why are you alone, and no one with you?"

2David said to Ahimelech the priest, "The king has charged me with a matter and said to me, 'Let no one know anything of the matter on which I am sending you and what I have commanded you.' I have told the young men to meet me at such and such a place.

3Now what do you have on hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever can be found."

4The priest answered David, "There is no common bread on hand, only holy bread, if only the young men have kept themselves from women."

5David answered the priest, "Women have indeed been kept from us, as always when I set out. The young men's vessels are holy even on an ordinary journey; how much more today will they be holy in their vessels!"

6So the priest gave him holy bread, for there was no bread there but the bread of the Presence, which had been taken away from before the LORD, to put hot bread in its place on the day it was taken away.

7Now one of Saul's servants was there that day, detained before the LORD. His name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief of Saul's shepherds.

8David said to Ahimelech, "Is there not a spear or a sword here on hand? For I did not bring my sword or my weapons with me, because the king's business was urgent."

9The priest said, "The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you struck down in the Valley of Elah, is here, wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you will take it, take it, for there is no other here but that one." David said, "There is none like it. Give it to me."

David Feigns Madness

10David rose and fled that day from Saul, and came to Achish king of Gath.

11The servants of Achish said to him, "Is this not David, the king of the land? Is this not the one they sang of to one another in the dances:
'Saul has struck down his thousands,
and David his ten thousands'?"

12David took these words to heart and was very afraid of Achish king of Gath.

13So he changed his behavior before them and acted like a madman in their hands. He scratched marks on the doors of the gate and let his spittle run down his beard.

14Achish said to his servants, "You see the man is mad. Why have you brought him to me?

15Do I lack madmen, that you have brought this one to act the madman before me? Shall this one come into my house?"

Notes

  • v1 "David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest" — in the Hebrew this is 21:2; from here to the end of the chapter the Hebrew numbering is one verse ahead of the English. Ahimelech is son of Ahitub (22:9), as Ahijah the priest was (14:3): the house of Eli, still serving. Came trembling to meet, va-yecherad… li-qrat, as the elders of Bethlehem met Samuel (16:4).

  • v2 "The king has charged me with a matter… such and such a place" — David lies to the priest, and the cost comes in 22:18–19. Peloni almoni, such and such, is the pair of words Boaz uses for the redeemer he will not name (Ruth 4:1).

  • vv4–5 "if only the young men have kept themselves from women" — the rule of Sinai, Do not go near a woman (Exodus 19:15), applied to men on campaign. David claims more than the priest asks: the men's vessels, their gear or their bodies, are holy on every march.

  • v6 "the bread of the Presence… hot bread in its place" — lechem ha-panim (Exodus 25:30), set out before the LORD and replaced fresh; the old bread shall be Aaron's and his sons', and they shall eat it in a holy place (Leviticus 24:9). Jesus cites this day when His disciples are charged with breaking the sabbath: David entered the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the bread of the Presence (Mark 2:26). Abiathar is Ahimelech's son, who escapes the slaughter of the priests (22:20).

  • v7 "Doeg the Edomite, the chief of Saul's shepherds" — ne'tsar lifnei YHWH, held back before the LORD, kept at the sanctuary for a reason the text does not give. An Edomite, of Esau's line, in Saul's service. What he sees here he reports (22:9), and he kills the priests (22:18). The Greek has Doeg the Syrian, who tended Saul's mules.

  • v9 "The sword of Goliath… wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod" — the sword David took from Goliath to cut off his head (17:51) and laid up (17:54) has been kept at the sanctuary. There is none like it: David had said the LORD saves not by sword and spear (17:47); now he flees with the Philistine's sword.

  • v10 "came to Achish king of Gath" — Gath is Goliath's town (17:4). David goes there carrying Goliath's sword.

  • v11 "Is this not David, the king of the land?" — the Philistines call him king before Israel does. The song of the women (18:7) has reached Gath.

  • v13 "he changed his behavior before them" — va-yeshanno et ta'mo, he changed his taste, his sense or judgment. Psalm 34 has the heading Of David, when he changed his behavior before Abimelech, who drove him out, and he went away, and the psalm says Taste and see that the LORD is good (34:8): the same ta'am. The Greek has he drummed on the doors of the city.

  • vv14–15 "Do I lack madmen?" — meshugga'im. The ruse works: Achish sees only one more madman, not the king of the land.

chapters.title: The Priests of Nob
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 22

The Cave of Adullam

1David left there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and all his father's house heard of it, they went down to him there.

2Everyone who was in distress, everyone who was in debt, and everyone who was bitter of soul gathered to him, and he became commander over them. There were about four hundred men with him.

3From there David went to Mizpeh of Moab and said to the king of Moab, "Please let my father and my mother come and stay with you until I know what God will do for me."

4He brought them before the king of Moab, and they stayed with him all the time that David was in the stronghold.

5Then Gad the prophet said to David, "Do not stay in the stronghold. Go, get into the land of Judah." So David went and came to the forest of Hereth.

Saul Accuses His Servants

6Saul heard that David and the men with him had been discovered. Saul was sitting at Gibeah under the tamarisk tree on the height, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing around him.

7Saul said to his servants standing around him, "Hear now, you Benjaminites! Will the son of Jesse give every one of you fields and vineyards? Will he make you all commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds,

8that all of you have conspired against me? No one tells me when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse. None of you is sorry for me or tells me that my son has stirred up my servant against me to lie in wait, as he does this day."

9Then Doeg the Edomite, who was standing over Saul's servants, answered, "I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech son of Ahitub.

10He inquired of the LORD for him and gave him provisions, and he gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine."

The Death of the Priests

11The king sent to summon Ahimelech the priest, son of Ahitub, and all his father's house, the priests who were at Nob, and all of them came to the king.

12Saul said, "Hear now, son of Ahitub." He said, "Here I am, my lord."

13Saul said to him, "Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, in that you gave him bread and a sword and inquired of God for him, so that he has risen against me to lie in wait, as he does this day?"

14Ahimelech answered the king, "Who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king's son-in-law, captain of your bodyguard and honored in your house?

15Is today the first time I have inquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let the king not charge his servant or all my father's house with anything, for your servant knew nothing of all this, little or great."

16The king said, "You shall die, Ahimelech, you and all your father's house."

17The king said to the runners standing around him, "Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because their hand also is with David, and they knew that he fled and did not tell me." But the king's servants would not put out their hands to strike the priests of the LORD.

18Then the king said to Doeg, "You turn and strike the priests." So Doeg the Edomite turned and struck the priests, and he killed that day eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.

19Nob, the city of the priests, he struck with the edge of the sword: man and woman, child and infant, ox and donkey and sheep, with the edge of the sword.

20But one son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub, whose name was Abiathar, escaped and fled after David.

21Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.

22David said to Abiathar, "I knew that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul. I am the cause of the death of every soul of your father's house.

23Stay with me; do not be afraid. The one who seeks my life seeks your life. With me you will be kept safe."

Notes

  • v2 "everyone who was in distress… in debt… bitter of soul" — mar nefesh, the words said of Hannah, she was bitter of soul (1:10).

  • vv3–4 "Mizpeh of Moab… my father and my mother" — David's great-grandmother was Ruth the Moabite: Obed was the father of Jesse, the father of David (Ruth 4:17). He takes his parents to the land she came from.

  • v7 "Will the son of Jesse give every one of you fields and vineyards? Will he make you all commanders of thousands" — Samuel's warning about the king: He will take the best of your fields and vineyards… and give them to his servants (8:14), and He will appoint for himself commanders of thousands (8:12). Saul now holds out that very bargain to his own tribe.

  • vv8, 13 "all of you have conspired against me" — qeshartem, from qashar, to bind, the verb of 18:1, the soul of Jonathan was bound to the soul of David. What was a bond of love Saul calls a conspiracy.

  • vv10, 15 "He inquired of the LORD for him… Is today the first time I have inquired of God for him?" — chapter 21 does not tell of an inquiry at Nob. Doeg reports one, and Ahimelech does not deny it: he says it was not the first.

  • v14 "as faithful as David" — ne'eman, the word of the LORD's promise to Eli, I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest (2:35), and of Samuel, established as a prophet (3:20). A priest of Eli's house uses it of David. Captain of your bodyguard, sar el mishma'tekha: David later sets Benaiah over his bodyguard, mishma'to (2 Samuel 23:23).

  • v17 "the king's servants would not put out their hands to strike the priests of the LORD" — the words David will use of Saul himself: far be it from me… to put out my hand against him, for he is the LORD's anointed (24:6). Only the Edomite does it.

  • v18 "eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod" — the ephod bad Samuel wore as a boy serving at Shiloh (2:18). The Greek has three hundred and five.

  • v19 "man and woman, child and infant, ox and donkey and sheep" — the list of the ban on Amalek, man and woman, child and infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey (15:3). Saul did not carry it out on Amalek; he carries it out on a city of the LORD's priests.

  • vv20–23 "one son of Ahimelech… escaped" — the word to Eli: The man of yours whom I do not cut off from My altar shall be spared to wear out your eyes (2:33). Abiathar serves David, and Solomon later removes him from the priesthood to fulfill the word of the LORD that He had spoken concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh (1 Kings 2:27).

chapters.title: Keilah and the Wilderness of Ziph
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 23

David Saves Keilah

1David was told, "The Philistines are fighting against Keilah and are plundering the threshing floors."

2So David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I go and strike these Philistines?" The LORD said to David, "Go, strike the Philistines and save Keilah."

3But David's men said to him, "We are afraid here in Judah. How much more if we go to Keilah against the ranks of the Philistines!"

4David inquired of the LORD again, and the LORD answered him, "Arise, go down to Keilah, for I am giving the Philistines into your hand."

5So David and his men went to Keilah and fought the Philistines. He drove off their livestock and struck them with a great slaughter. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.

6And it came to pass, when Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, that he came down with an ephod in his hand.

7Saul was told that David had come to Keilah. Saul said, "God has handed him over to me, for he has shut himself in by entering a town with gates and bars."

8Saul summoned all the people to war, to go down to Keilah and besiege David and his men.

9David knew that Saul was plotting evil against him, and he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod here."

10David said, "O LORD God of Israel, Your servant has heard for certain that Saul seeks to come to Keilah to destroy the town because of me.

11Will the lords of Keilah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down, as Your servant has heard? O LORD God of Israel, please tell Your servant." The LORD said, "He will come down."

12David said, "Will the lords of Keilah surrender me and my men into Saul's hand?" The LORD said, "They will surrender you."

13So David and his men, about six hundred, arose and left Keilah and went wherever they could go. When Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, he gave up the expedition.

Jonathan at Horesh

14David stayed in the wilderness, in the strongholds, in the hill country of the wilderness of Ziph. Saul sought him every day, but God did not give him into his hand.

15David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life. David was in the wilderness of Ziph, at Horesh.

16Jonathan, Saul's son, arose and went to David at Horesh and strengthened his hand in God.

17He said to him, "Do not be afraid, for the hand of Saul my father will not find you. You will be king over Israel, and I will be second to you. Saul my father also knows this."

18The two of them made a covenant before the LORD. David stayed at Horesh, and Jonathan went home.

The Ziphites

19Then the Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Is not David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah, which is south of Jeshimon?

20So, O king, come down whenever your soul desires to come down, and it will be our part to surrender him into the king's hand."

21Saul said, "Blessed are you by the LORD, for you have had pity on me.

22Go now, make sure once more. Find out and see the place where his foot rests, and who has seen him there, for I am told he is very shrewd.

23See and learn all the hiding places where he hides, and come back to me with sure word, and I will go with you. And it shall come to pass, if he is in the land, that I will search him out among all the clans of Judah."

24They arose and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah south of Jeshimon.

25Saul and his men went to seek him. When David was told, he went down to the rock and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. When Saul heard of it, he pursued David into the wilderness of Maon.

26Saul went on one side of the mountain, and David and his men on the other side of the mountain. David was hurrying to get away from Saul, while Saul and his men were closing in on David and his men to seize them.

27But a messenger came to Saul, saying, "Hurry and come, for the Philistines have made a raid on the land."

28So Saul turned back from pursuing David and went to meet the Philistines. That is why that place was called Sela-hammahlekoth.

29David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of En-gedi.

Notes

  • vv2, 4 "David inquired of the LORD… and the LORD answered him" — twice, and the answer comes both times. When Saul asked, He did not answer him that day (14:37), and at the end the LORD did not answer him, neither by dreams nor by Urim nor by prophets (28:6).

  • vv6, 9 "he came down with an ephod in his hand… Bring the ephod here" — the one priest who escaped Nob (22:20) brings the ephod to David. Saul killed the priests; the means of asking the LORD is now in David's camp.

  • vv7, 14 "God has handed him over to me… but God did not give him into his hand" — nikkar, made strange, handed over, a rare use of the word; the Greek has sold. Saul reads the LORD's will from the gates of Keilah. The narrator answers him in v14.

  • vv11–12 "Will the lords of Keilah surrender me?… They will surrender you" — ba'alei Qe'ilah, as the lords of Shechem. The town David has just saved would hand him over. The Greek has no v12 and gives the answer He will be shut in to the first question.

  • vv16–18 "strengthened his hand in God… I will be second to you" — le-mishneh, second: the king's son gives up the throne in words. This is the last time Jonathan and David meet. Jonathan dies with his father on Mount Gilboa (31:2).

  • v19 "Is not David hiding among us?" — the words of the heading of Psalm 54, when the Ziphites came and said to Saul, "Is not David hiding among us?"

  • v21 "for you have had pity on me" — chamaltem, the verb of 15:9, when Saul and the people spared Agag. Saul's pity went to the king of Amalek; now he asks it for himself.

  • v22 "I am told he is very shrewd" — arom ya'rim, from arum, the word of the serpent, shrewder than every living thing of the field (Genesis 3:1).

  • v28 "Sela-hammahlekoth" — sela, rock, and machleqot, from chalaq, to divide: the rock where the two sides parted. The same letters also mean smooth. The Greek has the Divided Rock.

  • v29 "the strongholds of En-gedi" — in the Hebrew this verse is 24:1, and chapter 24 runs one verse ahead of the English.

chapters.title: David Spares Saul at En-gedi
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 24

The Cave

1And it came to pass, when Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, that he was told, "David is in the wilderness of En-gedi."

2Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to seek David and his men in front of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.

3He came to the sheepfolds by the road, where there was a cave, and Saul went in to relieve himself. David and his men were sitting in the far recesses of the cave.

4David's men said to him, "This is the day of which the LORD said to you, 'I am giving your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as seems good in your eyes.'" Then David arose and secretly cut off the edge of Saul's robe.

5And it came to pass afterward that David's heart struck him because he had cut off the edge of Saul's robe.

6He said to his men, "The LORD forbid that I should do this thing to my lord, the LORD's anointed, to put out my hand against him, for he is the LORD's anointed."

7So David held his men back with these words and did not let them rise against Saul. Saul got up from the cave and went on his way.

"My Father, See"

8Afterward David also arose and went out of the cave and called after Saul, "My lord the king!" When Saul looked behind him, David bowed with his face to the ground and paid him homage.

9David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to the words of men who say, 'David is seeking to harm you'?

10This very day your eyes have seen how the LORD gave you into my hand in the cave. Some said to kill you, but I spared you. I said, 'I will not put out my hand against my lord, for he is the LORD's anointed.'

11My father, see, yes, see the edge of your robe in my hand. Since I cut off the edge of your robe and did not kill you, know and see that there is no evil or rebellion in my hand. I have not sinned against you, yet you are hunting my life to take it.

12May the LORD judge between me and you, and may the LORD avenge me on you; but my hand shall not be against you.

13As the proverb of the ancients says, 'From the wicked comes wickedness.' But my hand shall not be against you.

14After whom has the king of Israel come out? After whom are you chasing? After a dead dog! After a single flea!

15May the LORD be judge and judge between me and you, and may He see and plead my cause and deliver me from your hand."

Saul Weeps

16And it came to pass, when David had finished speaking these words to Saul, that Saul said, "Is this your voice, my son David?" Saul lifted up his voice and wept.

17He said to David, "You are more in the right than I, for you have repaid me with good, and I have repaid you with evil.

18You have shown today how you have dealt well with me: the LORD gave me into your hand, and you did not kill me.

19For if a man finds his enemy, will he let him go on his way safely? May the LORD repay you with good for what you have done to me this day.

20And now I know that you will surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hand.

21So swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my seed after me, and that you will not destroy my name from my father's house."

22So David swore to Saul. Saul went home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.

Notes

  • v1 "when Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines" — in the Hebrew this is 24:2; the whole chapter runs one verse ahead of the English, because the English puts 24:1 at the end of chapter 23.

  • v3 "Saul went in to relieve himself" — le-hasekh et raglav, to cover his feet, the phrase Eglon's servants used when they supposed he must be relieving himself (Judges 3:24). The king David is fleeing walks alone into David's hiding place.

  • v4 "This is the day of which the LORD said to you" — the LORD told David I am giving the Philistines into your hand (23:4); no such word about Saul has been told. His men make one out of it.

  • vv4–5 "cut off the edge of Saul's robe… David's heart struck him" — kenaf ha-me'il, the edge Saul tore from Samuel's robe when Samuel said, The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today (15:27–28). David cuts it from Saul's robe, and his own heart strikes him for it.

  • vv6, 10 "to put out my hand against him, for he is the LORD's anointed" — mashiach YHWH. David will ask the Amalekite who claims to have killed Saul, How were you not afraid to put out your hand to destroy the LORD's anointed? (2 Samuel 1:14).

  • v7 "David held his men back with these words" — va-yeshassa, a verb of tearing apart, used of Samson, who tore the lion as one tears a young goat (Judges 14:6).

  • vv11, 16 "My father, see… Is this your voice, my son David?" — the son-in-law calls the king my father. Saul, who has called him only the son of Jesse (20:27–31, 22:7–13), answers my son David.

  • v14 "After a dead dog! After a single flea!" — the Philistine asked, Am I a dog? (17:43). David calls himself a dead dog; Mephibosheth will say a dead dog such as I to King David (2 Samuel 9:8).

  • v17 "You are more in the right than I" — tsaddiq attah mimmenni, the words of Judah over Tamar, She is more in the right than I (Genesis 38:26): the one in power admits the one he wronged was right.

  • vv20–21 "you will surely be king… you will not cut off my seed after me" — Jonathan had said, Saul my father also knows this (23:17), and asked the same oath for his house (20:15). David spares Jonathan's son because of the oath of the LORD (2 Samuel 21:7), but in the same chapter he hands over seven other sons and grandsons of Saul (2 Samuel 21:8–9).

chapters.title: Nabal and Abigail
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 25

The Death of Samuel

1Samuel died. All Israel gathered and mourned for him, and they buried him at his house in Ramah. Then David arose and went down to the wilderness of Paran.

Nabal

2There was a man in Maon whose business was at Carmel. The man was very rich; he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats. He was shearing his sheep at Carmel.

3The name of the man was Nabal, and the name of his wife Abigail. The woman was of good understanding and beautiful, but the man was harsh and evil in his dealings. He was a Calebite.

4David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.

5So David sent ten young men. David said to the young men, "Go up to Carmel, go to Nabal and greet him in my name.

6Say this: 'Long life to you! Peace to you, peace to your house, and peace to all that you have.

7Now I have heard that you have shearers. Your shepherds have been with us, and we did not humiliate them, and nothing of theirs was missing all the time they were in Carmel.

8Ask your young men, and they will tell you. So let my young men find favor in your eyes, for we have come on a feast day. Please give whatever you have at hand to your servants and to your son David.'"

9When David's young men came, they said all these words to Nabal in David's name, and they waited.

10Nabal answered David's servants, "Who is David? Who is the son of Jesse? There are many servants these days who are breaking away, each from his master.

11Shall I take my bread and my water and the meat I have slaughtered for my shearers and give it to men who come from I do not know where?"

12So David's young men turned on their way and went back, and came and told him all these words.

13David said to his men, "Every man strap on his sword!" Every man strapped on his sword, and David also strapped on his sword. About four hundred men went up after David, and two hundred stayed with the baggage.

Abigail

14One of the young men told Abigail, Nabal's wife, "David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, and he flew at them.

15Yet the men were very good to us. We were not humiliated, and we missed nothing all the time we went about with them when we were in the field.

16They were a wall to us both by night and by day, all the time we were with them keeping the sheep.

17So know and consider what you should do, for evil has been resolved against our master and against all his house. He is such a worthless man that no one can speak to him."

18Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves, two skins of wine, five sheep ready dressed, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred clusters of raisins and two hundred cakes of figs, and loaded them on donkeys.

19She said to her young men, "Go on ahead of me; I am coming after you." But she did not tell her husband Nabal.

20As she rode on the donkey and came down under cover of the mountain, David and his men were coming down toward her, and she met them.

21Now David had said, "It was all for nothing that I guarded everything this man has in the wilderness, so that nothing of all he has was missing. He has repaid me evil for good.

22May God do so to the enemies of David, and more also, if by morning I leave so much as one male of all who belong to him."

23When Abigail saw David, she hurried and got down from the donkey, fell on her face before David and bowed to the ground.

24She fell at his feet and said, "On me alone, my lord, be the guilt. Please let your servant speak in your ears, and hear the words of your servant.

25Please let my lord not set his heart on this worthless man, Nabal, for as his name is, so is he: Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. But I, your servant, did not see the young men of my lord whom you sent.

26And now, my lord, as the LORD lives and as your soul lives, since the LORD has kept you from coming into bloodguilt and from saving yourself with your own hand, and now let your enemies and those who seek evil against my lord be like Nabal.

27Now let this gift that your servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who follow my lord.

28Please forgive the offense of your servant. For the LORD will surely make my lord a sure house, because my lord is fighting the battles of the LORD, and evil shall not be found in you all your days.

29If a man rises up to pursue you and to seek your life, the life of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God, and the lives of your enemies He shall sling out as from the hollow of a sling.

30And it shall come to pass, when the LORD has done for my lord all the good He has spoken concerning you, and has appointed you leader over Israel,

31that this will not be a stumbling block to you, or a burden on my lord's heart, that you shed blood without cause or that my lord saved himself. When the LORD has dealt well with my lord, remember your servant."

32David said to Abigail, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you this day to meet me!

33Blessed be your discernment, and blessed be you, who have kept me this day from coming into bloodguilt and from saving myself with my own hand!

34For truly, as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who has kept me from harming you, if you had not hurried and come to meet me, surely by morning light there would not have been left to Nabal so much as one male."

35Then David received from her hand what she had brought him, and he said to her, "Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice and granted your request."

The Death of Nabal

36Abigail came to Nabal, and there he was, holding a feast in his house like the feast of a king. Nabal's heart was merry within him, and he was very drunk, so she told him nothing at all until morning light.

37And it came to pass in the morning, when the wine had gone out of Nabal, that his wife told him these things, and his heart died within him, and he became like a stone.

38And it came to pass about ten days later that the LORD struck Nabal, and he died.

39When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, "Blessed be the LORD, who has pleaded the cause of my disgrace at the hand of Nabal, and has kept His servant back from evil. The LORD has returned the evil of Nabal on his own head." Then David sent and spoke to Abigail, to take her as his wife.

40David's servants came to Abigail at Carmel and said to her, "David has sent us to you to take you to him as his wife."

41She arose and bowed with her face to the ground and said, "Your servant is a maidservant to wash the feet of my lord's servants."

42Abigail hurried and arose and rode on a donkey, with her five young women who attended her. She went after David's messengers and became his wife.

43David had also taken Ahinoam of Jezreel, and both of them became his wives.

44But Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.

Notes

  • v1 "Samuel died… the wilderness of Paran" — the man who anointed both kings dies between the two sparings of Saul (chapters 24 and 26). Paran is the wilderness where Israel camped after leaving Sinai (Numbers 10:12). The Greek has the wilderness of Maon, the place named in the next verse.

  • v3 "He was a Calebite" — the written text has kelibbo, as his heart, and the reading is kalibbi, a Calebite, of the clan of Caleb, who was given his portion in Judah (Joshua 15:13). Kelev is dog, and the Greek reads it so: the man was doglike.

  • vv3, 25, 37 "Nabal… folly is with him… when the wine had gone out of Nabal" — naval is fool, as in The fool says in his heart, "There is no God" (Psalm 14:1), and nevalah is folly. The same letters make nevel, the skin of wine Abigail loads in v18. The wine goes out of Nabal, and his heart dies.

  • v10 "Who is David? Who is the son of Jesse?" — Saul's contempt, the son of Jesse, in the mouth of a rich man of Judah, David's own tribe. The form of the question is Pharaoh's: Who is the LORD, that I should listen to His voice? (Exodus 5:2).

  • v22 "May God do so to the enemies of David… so much as one male" — an oath of this kind calls the curse down on the speaker (May the LORD do so to me, Ruth 1:17). The Hebrew has to the enemies of David, turning the curse away from David; the Greek has to David. One male is literally one who urinates against the wall, the Hebrew idiom for a man or boy (also v34).

  • vv26, 31, 33, 39 "from saving yourself with your own hand" — the danger Gideon was warned of, that Israel would say My own hand has saved me (Judges 7:2). Abigail keeps David from it, and when the LORD strikes Nabal, David says He has pleaded the cause of my disgrace, the words he had used to Saul, may He see and plead my cause (24:15).

  • v28 "the LORD will surely make my lord a sure house" — bayit ne'eman, what the LORD promised the faithful priest in place of Eli, I will build him a sure house (2:35), and what Nathan will promise David, your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever (2 Samuel 7:16). Abigail says it first.

  • v29 "bound in the bundle of the living… sling out as from the hollow of a sling" — tseror ha-chayyim, the bundle in which something precious is tied and kept. The enemies' lives are flung away like stones; the sling is the weapon that killed Goliath (17:49–50).

  • v33 "Blessed be your discernment" — ta'mekh, your taste, your judgment, the word of 21:13, when David changed his behavior before Achish.

  • v44 "Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Palti" — David later demands her back, and Paltiel went with her, weeping behind her, until Abner sent him home (2 Samuel 3:15–16).

Nabal answered David's servants, "Who is David? Who is the son of Jesse? There are many servants these days who are breaking away, each from his master.
Shall I take my bread and my water and the meat I have slaughtered for my shearers and give it to men who come from I do not know where?"
So David's young men turned on their way and went back, and came and told him all these words.

David said to his men, "Every man strap on his sword!" Every man strapped on his sword, and David also strapped on his sword. About four hundred men went up after David, and two hundred stayed with the baggage.
Abigail
One of the young men told Abigail, Nabal's wife, "David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, and he flew at them.
Yet the men were very good to us. We were not humiliated, and we missed nothing all the time we went about with them when we were in the field.
They were a wall to us both by night and by day, all the time we were with them keeping the sheep.
So know and consider what you should do, for evil has been resolved against our master and against all his house. He is such a worthless man that no one can speak to him."

Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves, two skins of wine, five sheep ready dressed, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred clusters of raisins and two hundred cakes of figs, and loaded them on donkeys.
She said to her young men, "Go on ahead of me; I am coming after you." But she did not tell her husband Nabal.
As she rode on the donkey and came down under cover of the mountain, David and his men were coming down toward her, and she met them.
Now David had said, "It was all for nothing that I guarded everything this man has in the wilderness, so that nothing of all he has was missing. He has repaid me evil for good.
May God do so to the enemies of David, and more also, if by morning I leave so much as one male of all who belong to him."
When Abigail saw David, she hurried and got down from the donkey, fell on her face before David and bowed to the ground.
She fell at his feet and said, "On me alone, my lord, be the guilt. Please let your servant speak in your ears, and hear the words of your servant.

Please let my lord not set his heart on this worthless man, Nabal, for as his name is, so is he: Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. But I, your servant, did not see the young men of my lord whom you sent.

And now, my lord, as the LORD lives and as your soul lives, since the LORD has kept you from coming into bloodguilt and from saving yourself with your own hand, and now let your enemies and those who seek evil against my lord be like Nabal.
Now let this gift that your servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who follow my lord.
Please forgive the offense of your servant. For the LORD will surely make my lord a sure house, because my lord is fighting the battles of the LORD, and evil shall not be found in you all your days.

If a man rises up to pursue you and to seek your life, the life of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God, and the lives of your enemies He shall sling out as from the hollow of a sling.
And it shall come to pass, when the LORD has done for my lord all the good He has spoken concerning you, and has appointed you leader over Israel,

that this will not be a stumbling block to you, or a burden on my lord's heart, that you shed blood without cause or that my lord saved himself. When the LORD has dealt well with my lord, remember your servant."
David said to Abigail, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you this day to meet me!
Blessed be your discernment, and blessed be you, who have kept me this day from coming into bloodguilt and from saving myself with my own hand!

For truly, as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who has kept me from harming you, if you had not hurried and come to meet me, surely by morning light there would not have been left to Nabal so much as one male."
Then David received from her hand what she had brought him, and he said to her, "Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice and granted your request."
The Death of Nabal

Abigail came to Nabal, and there he was, holding a feast in his house like the feast of a king. Nabal's heart was merry within him, and he was very drunk, so she told him nothing at all until morning light.
And it came to pass in the morning, when the wine had gone out of Nabal, that his wife told him these things, and his heart died within him, and he became like a stone.
And it came to pass about ten days later that the LORD struck Nabal, and he died.

When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, "Blessed be the LORD, who has pleaded the cause of my disgrace at the hand of Nabal, and has kept His servant back from evil. The LORD has returned the evil of Nabal on his own head." Then David sent and spoke to Abigail, to take her as his wife.
David's servants came to Abigail at Carmel and said to her, "David has sent us to you to take you to him as his wife."
She arose and bowed with her face to the ground and said, "Your servant is a maidservant to wash the feet of my lord's servants."
Abigail hurried and arose and rode on a donkey, with her five young women who attended her. She went after David's messengers and became his wife.
David had also taken Ahinoam of Jezreel, and both of them became his wives.
But Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.

chapters.title: David Spares Saul Again
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 26

The Spear and the Water Jar

1The Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Is not David hiding on the hill of Hachilah, facing Jeshimon?"

2So Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph with three thousand chosen men of Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.

3Saul camped on the hill of Hachilah, which faces Jeshimon, by the road. David was staying in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.

4David sent out spies and learned that Saul had indeed come.

5Then David arose and came to the place where Saul had camped. David saw the place where Saul lay, with Abner son of Ner, the commander of his army. Saul was lying inside the encampment, and the army was camped around him.

6David said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, "Who will go down with me to Saul in the camp?" Abishai said, "I will go down with you."

7So David and Abishai came to the army by night. Saul lay sleeping inside the encampment, with his spear stuck in the ground at his head, and Abner and the army were lying around him.

8Abishai said to David, "God has delivered your enemy into your hand today. Now please let me pin him to the ground with the spear in one stroke; I will not need to strike him twice."

9But David said to Abishai, "Do not destroy him, for who can put out his hand against the LORD's anointed and be guiltless?"

10David said, "As the LORD lives, the LORD will strike him; or his day will come and he will die; or he will go down into battle and perish.

11The LORD forbid that I should put out my hand against the LORD's anointed. But now take the spear that is at his head and the water jar, and let us go."

12So David took the spear and the water jar from Saul's head, and they went away. No one saw it, no one knew it, and no one woke, for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them.

"Is This Your Voice, My Son David?"

13Then David crossed over to the other side and stood on top of the mountain far off, with a great space between them.

14David called to the army and to Abner son of Ner, "Will you not answer, Abner?" Abner answered, "Who are you, calling to the king?"

15David said to Abner, "Are you not a man? Who is like you in Israel? Why then have you not kept watch over your lord the king? For one of the people came in to destroy the king your lord.

16This thing that you have done is not good. As the LORD lives, you deserve to die, because you have not kept watch over your lord, the LORD's anointed. Now see where the king's spear is, and the water jar that was at his head."

17Saul recognized David's voice and said, "Is this your voice, my son David?" David said, "It is my voice, my lord the king."

18He said, "Why is my lord pursuing his servant? What have I done? What evil is in my hand?

19Now let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If it is the LORD who has stirred you up against me, may He accept an offering; but if it is men, cursed be they before the LORD, for they have driven me out this day from having a share in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, 'Go, serve other gods.'

20So do not let my blood fall to the ground away from the presence of the LORD, for the king of Israel has come out to seek a single flea, as one hunts a partridge in the mountains."

21Saul said, "I have sinned. Return, my son David, for I will not harm you again, because my life was precious in your eyes this day. I have acted foolishly and have erred very greatly."

22David answered, "Here is the king's spear! Let one of the young men come over and take it.

23The LORD will repay each man for his righteousness and his faithfulness. The LORD gave you into my hand today, but I would not put out my hand against the LORD's anointed.

24As your life was highly valued this day in my eyes, so may my life be highly valued in the eyes of the LORD, and may He deliver me from all trouble."

25Saul said to David, "Blessed are you, my son David! You will do great things and will surely prevail." So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

Notes

  • v1 "Is not David hiding on the hill of Hachilah?" — the Ziphites' second report (23:19). The chapter runs close to chapter 24: Saul hunts with three thousand men, is given into David's hand, is spared, and calls David my son.

  • vv7, 8, 11 "his spear stuck in the ground at his head… let me pin him to the ground with the spear" — the spear Saul threw to pin David to the wall (18:11), threw again (19:10), and threw at his own son (20:33). Abishai offers to pin Saul with it, ba-chanit u-va-arets, as Saul said be-David u-va-qir. David takes it away instead.

  • v10 "the LORD will strike him; or his day will come… or he will go down into battle and perish" — yiggafennu, the verb of the previous chapter, the LORD struck Nabal, and he died (25:38). David leaves Saul's death to the LORD. The third way is the one that comes: Saul dies in battle on Gilboa (31:3–4).

  • v12 "a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them" — tardemah, the sleep the LORD God made fall on the first man (Genesis 2:21) and the sleep that fell on Abram at the covenant (Genesis 15:12). The whole army sleeps by the LORD's doing.

  • v16 "you deserve to die" — benei mavet, the words Saul used of David, he deserves to die (20:31). David turns them on the men who were supposed to guard the king.

  • v19 "may He accept an offering… Go, serve other gods" — yarach minchah, may He smell an offering, as the LORD smelled the soothing aroma after the flood (Genesis 8:21). To be driven from the LORD's inheritance is to be sent where one must serve other gods, the exile the law foresaw: There you will serve gods made by human hands (Deuteronomy 4:28).

  • vv14, 20 "Who are you, calling to the king?… as one hunts a partridge" — ha-qore, the partridge, is literally the caller. Abner asked Who are you who calls, qarata, and David, calling from the hilltop, names himself the bird that calls on the mountains.

  • v21 "I have acted foolishly" — hiskalti, the word Samuel spoke to Saul at Gilgal, You have acted foolishly (13:13). Now Saul says it of himself.

  • vv21, 24 "my life was precious in your eyes… as your life was highly valued" — Saul says yaqrah, precious; David answers gadlah, great, and asks for the same from the LORD.

  • v25 "You will do great things and will surely prevail" — these are the last words Saul and David speak to each other. David goes his way; Saul returns to his place.

chapters.title: David Among the Philistines
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 27

Ziklag

1David said in his heart, "Now I shall perish one day by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than to escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will give up seeking me any longer in all the territory of Israel, and I shall escape from his hand."

2So David arose and crossed over, he and the six hundred men with him, to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath.

3David stayed with Achish at Gath, he and his men, each with his household, and David with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel, and Abigail of Carmel, Nabal's widow.

4When Saul was told that David had fled to Gath, he no longer sought him.

5David said to Achish, "If I have found favor in your eyes, let a place be given me in one of the country towns, so that I may live there. Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?"

6So that day Achish gave him Ziklag. That is why Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.

7The time that David lived in the country of the Philistines was a year and four months.

The Raids

8David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Gizrites and the Amalekites, for these were the inhabitants of the land from of old, as you go to Shur and as far as the land of Egypt.

9David struck the land and left neither man nor woman alive, and he took sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels and clothing, and came back to Achish.

10When Achish asked, "Where have you raided today?" David would say, "Against the Negev of Judah," or "Against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites," or "Against the Negev of the Kenites."

11David left neither man nor woman alive to bring to Gath, thinking, "In case they tell about us, saying, 'This is what David did.'" This was his practice all the time he lived in the country of the Philistines.

12Achish trusted David, thinking, "He has made himself utterly hateful to his people Israel, and he will be my servant forever."

Notes

  • v1 "Now I shall perish one day by the hand of Saul" — espeh, the verb David used of Saul in the last chapter, he will go down into battle and perish (26:10). After two sparings and two promises from Saul, David despairs of the promises and leaves the land.

  • v2 "Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath" — the king before whom David played the madman (21:10–15). He comes back with six hundred men, not alone; the Greek has four hundred.

  • v6 "Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day" — Ziklag was given to Judah in Joshua's allotment and then to Simeon (Joshua 15:31, 19:5); here a Philistine king gives it to David. The kings of Judah is written from a time when Judah had kings of its own.

  • v7 "a year and four months" — yamim ve-arba'ah chodashim, days and four months. Yamim, days, can mean a full year, as in the yearly sacrifice, zevach ha-yamim (1:21). The Greek has four months.

  • vv8–9 "the Geshurites, the Gizrites and the Amalekites… left neither man nor woman alive" — the Geshurites are among the peoples of the land that remains in Joshua's day (Joshua 13:2). David does to the Amalekites what Saul was commanded to do and did not (15:3, 15:9), though he keeps the livestock.

  • vv10–11 "Against the Negev of Judah… In case they tell about us" — a lie to his Philistine lord. He names his own tribe and the Kenites, whom Saul had warned away from Amalek (15:6). None are left alive to contradict him.

  • v12 "He has made himself utterly hateful to his people Israel" — hav'esh hiv'ish, he has made himself stink, the word of 13:4, when Israel has also become a stench to the Philistines. My servant forever, eved olam, are the words of the law for a slave who chooses to stay with his master: he shall be your slave forever (Deuteronomy 15:17).

chapters.title: Saul at En-dor
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 28

Philistines at Shunem

1And it came to pass in those days that the Philistines gathered their forces for war, to fight against Israel. Achish said to David, "Know for certain that you and your men shall go out with me in the army."

2David said to Achish, "Very well, you shall know what your servant will do." Achish said to David, "Very well, I will make you my bodyguard for life."

3Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, his own town. Saul had removed the ghosts and the spirits from the land.

4The Philistines gathered and came and camped at Shunem, and Saul gathered all Israel, and they camped at Gilboa.

5When Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.

6Saul inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him, neither by dreams nor by Urim nor by prophets.

The Woman at En-dor

7Then Saul said to his servants, "Find me a woman who has a ghost, so that I may go to her and inquire of her." His servants said to him, "There is a woman who has a ghost at En-dor."

8So Saul disguised himself and put on other clothes, and he went with two men, and they came to the woman by night. He said, "Practice soothsaying for me by the ghost, and bring up for me the one I name to you."

9The woman said to him, "Surely you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off the ghosts and the spirits from the land. Why then are you laying a snare for my life, to bring about my death?"

10Saul swore to her by the LORD, "As the LORD lives, no punishment shall come upon you for this."

11Then the woman said, "Whom shall I bring up for you?" He said, "Bring up Samuel for me."

12When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out with a loud voice, and the woman said to Saul, "Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!"

13The king said to her, "Do not be afraid. What do you see?" The woman said to Saul, "I see a god coming up out of the earth."

14He said to her, "What does he look like?" She said, "An old man is coming up, and he is wrapped in a robe." Then Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed with his face to the ground and paid homage.

Samuel's Word

15Samuel said to Saul, "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?" Saul said, "I am in great distress. The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has departed from me and no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I have called you to tell me what I should do."

16Samuel said, "Why then do you ask me, since the LORD has departed from you and has become your adversary?

17The LORD has done as He spoke by me. The LORD has torn the kingdom out of your hand and given it to your neighbor, to David.

18Because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD and did not carry out His fierce anger against Amalek, the LORD has done this thing to you today.

19The LORD will also give Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The LORD will also give the army of Israel into the hand of the Philistines."

20At once Saul fell full length on the ground, terrified by Samuel's words. There was no strength left in him, for he had eaten no food all day and all night.

21The woman came to Saul and saw that he was badly shaken, and she said to him, "Your servant has listened to your voice. I took my life in my hand and listened to the words you spoke to me.

22So now, please, listen also to the voice of your servant. Let me set a morsel of bread before you, and eat, so that you may have strength when you go on your way."

23He refused and said, "I will not eat." But his servants, together with the woman, pressed him, and he listened to their voice. He rose from the ground and sat on the bed.

24The woman had a fattened calf in the house, and she quickly slaughtered it. She took flour, kneaded it and baked unleavened bread.

25She set it before Saul and his servants, and they ate. Then they rose and went away that night.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "you shall know what your servant will do… I will make you my bodyguard for life" — David's answer can be heard two ways, and Achish hears it as loyalty. The next chapter decides it without David having to choose.

  • vv3, 9 "Saul had removed the ghosts and the spirits from the land" — ha-ovot ve-ha-yidde'onim, the words of the law, Do not turn to ghosts, and do not seek out spirits (Leviticus 19:31). The words name both the spirit consulted and the one who consults it. Saul had kept this law.

  • v6 "neither by dreams nor by Urim nor by prophets" — every lawful way of asking. David has the ephod and the priest (23:6, 23:9), and the LORD answers him. Saul had been left unanswered before (14:37). Chronicles names this night among the causes of his death: Saul died for his unfaithfulness… and also for asking a ghost, to inquire of it, and he did not inquire of the LORD (1 Chronicles 10:13–14).

  • v7 "a woman who has a ghost" — eshet ba'alat ov, a woman, mistress of a ghost, as the law says a man or a woman who has a ghost or a spirit in them shall surely be put to death (Leviticus 20:27).

  • v8 "Practice soothsaying for me by the ghost… the one I name to you" — qosomi, the practice Samuel set beside rebellion: rebellion is the sin of soothsaying (15:23). The one I name to you are the LORD's words to Samuel when He sent him to anoint David (16:3).

  • v13 "I see a god coming up out of the earth" — elohim, with a plural verb, olim: a divine being, or gods. The Greek has gods. The word is the ordinary word for God; here it names what the woman sees rising.

  • v14 "an old man… wrapped in a robe" — me'il, the robe Hannah made Samuel as a boy (2:19) and the robe Saul tore when the kingdom was torn from him (15:27–28). Saul knows him by it.

  • vv16–19 "has become your adversary… torn the kingdom… tomorrow you and your sons will be with me" — Samuel repeats his word at Gilgal, The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you (15:28), and the cause, Amalek (15:18). The Greek of v16 has has become with your neighbor. Tomorrow comes in 31:6: Saul died, and his three sons… on that day together. Arekha, your adversary, is a rare word; the same form stands in Psalm 139:20.

  • vv21–25 "I took my life in my hand… a fattened calf… unleavened bread" — the woman risks her life for the king who outlawed her, and then feeds him. The meal is made in haste, as Abraham made one for his guests (Genesis 18:6–7).

Saul swore to her by the LORD, "As the LORD lives, no punishment shall come upon you for this."
Then the woman said, "Whom shall I bring up for you?" He said, "Bring up Samuel for me."
When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out with a loud voice, and the woman said to Saul, "Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!"
The king said to her, "Do not be afraid. What do you see?" The woman said to Saul, "I see a god coming up out of the earth."

He said to her, "What does he look like?" She said, "An old man is coming up, and he is wrapped in a robe." Then Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed with his face to the ground and paid homage.
Samuel's Word

Samuel said to Saul, "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?" Saul said, "I am in great distress. The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has departed from me and no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I have called you to tell me what I should do."
Samuel said, "Why then do you ask me, since the LORD has departed from you and has become your adversary?
The LORD has done as He spoke by me. The LORD has torn the kingdom out of your hand and given it to your neighbor, to David.
Because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD and did not carry out His fierce anger against Amalek, the LORD has done this thing to you today.
The LORD will also give Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The LORD will also give the army of Israel into the hand of the Philistines."
At once Saul fell full length on the ground, terrified by Samuel's words. There was no strength left in him, for he had eaten no food all day and all night.
The woman came to Saul and saw that he was badly shaken, and she said to him, "Your servant has listened to your voice. I took my life in my hand and listened to the words you spoke to me.
So now, please, listen also to the voice of your servant. Let me set a morsel of bread before you, and eat, so that you may have strength when you go on your way."
He refused and said, "I will not eat." But his servants, together with the woman, pressed him, and he listened to their voice. He rose from the ground and sat on the bed.
The woman had a fattened calf in the house, and she quickly slaughtered it. She took flour, kneaded it and baked unleavened bread.
She set it before Saul and his servants, and they ate. Then they rose and went away that night.

chapters.title: David Sent Back from the Philistine Army
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 29

"What Are These Hebrews?"

1The Philistines gathered all their forces at Aphek, and Israel was camped by the spring in Jezreel.

2The lords of the Philistines were passing on by hundreds and by thousands, and David and his men were passing on in the rear with Achish.

3The commanders of the Philistines said, "What are these Hebrews?" Achish said to the commanders of the Philistines, "Is this not David, the servant of Saul king of Israel, who has been with me these days, or these years? I have found nothing against him from the day he came over to me until this day."

4But the commanders of the Philistines were angry with him, and the commanders of the Philistines said to him, "Send the man back, so that he may return to the place you assigned him. He shall not go down with us into battle, or he will become an adversary to us in the battle. For how could this man win back his lord's favor? Would it not be with the heads of these men?

5Is this not David, of whom they sang to one another in the dances:
'Saul has struck down his thousands,
and David his ten thousands'?"

Achish Sends David Away

6Then Achish called David and said to him, "As the LORD lives, you have been upright, and your going out and coming in with me in the army is good in my eyes, for I have found no evil in you from the day you came to me until this day. But in the eyes of the lords you are not good.

7So now go back, and go in peace, so that you do nothing that is evil in the eyes of the lords of the Philistines."

8David said to Achish, "But what have I done? What have you found in your servant from the day I entered your service until this day, that I may not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?"

9Achish answered David, "I know that you are as good in my eyes as a messenger of God. But the commanders of the Philistines have said, 'He shall not go up with us into the battle.'

10So now rise early in the morning with the servants of your lord who came with you. Rise early in the morning, and as soon as you have light, go."

11So David rose early, he and his men, to go in the morning and return to the land of the Philistines, while the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

Notes

  • v1 "at Aphek" — where the Philistines camped when they took the ark (4:1). The book's first Philistine victory and its last are gathered from the same place.

  • v3 "What are these Hebrews?" — the Philistines' name for Israel (4:6, 13:19, 14:11). Achish answers with a name the commanders know better: David, the servant of Saul.

  • v4 "or he will become an adversary to us" — satan, adversary, the word used of the messenger of the LORD who took his stand in the road as an adversary against Balaam (Numbers 22:22). The heads of these men recalls the head David carried from the Valley of Elah (17:54, 17:57).

  • v5 "Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands" — the song of the women (18:7), quoted by the servants of Achish when David first came to Gath (21:11), and now by the Philistine commanders. It follows David everywhere among the Philistines.

  • v6 "As the LORD lives" — the Philistine king swears by the LORD's name to David.

  • v8 "that I may not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king" — which king David means is not said. Achish hears himself; my lord the king is also what David called Saul at En-gedi (24:8). The commanders' fear in v4 is the other reading.

  • v9 "as good in my eyes as a messenger of God" — ke-mal'akh Elohim. The same comparison is made of David as king by the woman of Tekoa (2 Samuel 14:17) and by Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 19:27).

  • v11 "while the Philistines went up to Jezreel" — David is sent away before the battle in which Saul dies (31:1–6). The Philistine lords' distrust keeps him from fighting Israel and from fighting for it.

chapters.title: David Recovers Ziklag's Captives
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 30

Ziklag Burned

1And it came to pass, when David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had made a raid on the Negev and on Ziklag. They had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire,

2and had taken captive the women who were in it, from the least to the greatest. They killed no one, but carried them off and went their way.

3When David and his men came to the town, it had been burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.

4David and the people with him lifted up their voices and wept until they had no strength left to weep.

5David's two wives had been taken captive, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel.

6David was in great distress, for the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was bitter, each for his sons and his daughters. But David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.

The Pursuit

7David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, "Bring me the ephod." Abiathar brought the ephod to David.

8David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I pursue this raiding band? Shall I overtake them?" He said to him, "Pursue, for you will overtake them and you will rescue."

9So David went, he and the six hundred men with him, and they came to the Wadi Besor, where those who were left behind stayed.

10David pursued, he and four hundred men; two hundred men stayed behind, who were too exhausted to cross the Wadi Besor.

11They found an Egyptian in the open country and brought him to David. They gave him bread, and he ate, and they gave him water to drink.

12They gave him a piece of a cake of figs and two clusters of raisins, and when he had eaten, his spirit came back to him, for he had not eaten bread or drunk water for three days and three nights.

13David said to him, "To whom do you belong, and where are you from?" He said, "I am a young Egyptian, the slave of an Amalekite. My master left me behind because I fell sick three days ago.

14We made a raid on the Negev of the Cherethites, on what belongs to Judah and on the Negev of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag with fire."

15David said to him, "Will you take me down to this band?" He said, "Swear to me by God that you will not kill me or hand me over to my master, and I will take you down to this band."

16When he had taken him down, there they were, spread out over all the land, eating and drinking and feasting on all the great spoil they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.

17David struck them from twilight until the evening of the next day, and not a man of them escaped except four hundred young men who rode off on camels and fled.

18David recovered all that the Amalekites had taken, and David rescued his two wives.

19Nothing of theirs was missing, small or great, sons or daughters, spoil or anything they had taken for themselves. David brought everything back.

20David took all the flocks and the herds. They drove them ahead of the other livestock and said, "This is David's spoil."

Equal Shares

21Then David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow David, whom they had left at the Wadi Besor. They came out to meet David and the people who were with him, and David came near to the people and greeted them.

22Then all the wicked and worthless men among those who had gone with David answered, "Because they did not go with us, we will not give them any of the spoil we have recovered, except for each man's wife and children. Let them lead them away and go."

23But David said, "You shall not do so, my brothers, with what the LORD has given us. He has kept us and has given into our hand the band that came against us.

24Who would listen to you in this? For as is the share of the one who goes down into the battle, so shall be the share of the one who stays with the baggage; they shall share alike."

25And it came to pass from that day forward that he made it a statute and a rule for Israel, to this day.

26When David came to Ziklag, he sent some of the spoil to the elders of Judah, his friends, saying, "Here is a gift for you from the spoil of the enemies of the LORD":

27to those in Bethel, in Ramoth of the Negev and in Jattir,

28to those in Aroer, in Siphmoth and in Eshtemoa,

29to those in Racal, in the towns of the Jerahmeelites and in the towns of the Kenites,

30to those in Hormah, in Bor-ashan and in Athach,

31to those in Hebron, and to all the places where David and his men had gone about.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "the Amalekites had made a raid… They killed no one" — the people David raided from Ziklag (27:8), leaving neither man nor woman alive (27:9, 27:11). The Amalekites raid Ziklag in return and take everyone alive.

  • v6 "the soul of all the people was bitter… But David strengthened himself in the LORD his God" — marah nefesh, the bitterness of the men who first gathered to David (22:2). Va-yitchazzeq, strengthened himself, the verb of Jonathan, who strengthened his hand in God (23:16). Now there is no Jonathan, and David does it himself.

  • vv7–8 "Bring me the ephod… Pursue, for you will overtake them" — the night before, Saul asked and the LORD did not answer him (28:6). David asks and is answered.

  • vv11–13 "an Egyptian… My master left me behind because I fell sick" — the Amalekite abandons his sick slave; David's men feed him, and he leads them to his master's camp. His spirit came back to him, va-tashov rucho: food and water restore him.

  • v17 "except four hundred young men who rode off on camels" — four hundred, the number who went with David (v10). Amalek, whom Saul was to destroy (15:3), is struck again but not ended.

  • v22 "all the wicked and worthless men" — ish ra u-veliyya'al. Beliyya'al, worthless, is the word used of Nabal (25:17, 25:25) and of the men who despised Saul (10:27).

  • vv24–25 "they shall share alike… a statute and a rule for Israel" — the law of the plunder of Midian divided it between those who took part in the battle… and the whole congregation (Numbers 31:27). Choq u-mishpat, a statute and a rule, as at Marah, There He made for them a statute and a rule (Exodus 15:25). David, not yet king, makes law for Israel.

  • v26 "a gift for you from the spoil of the enemies of the LORD" — berakhah, blessing, the word Abigail used for her gift to David (25:27). The enemies of the LORD: David calls his wars what Saul asked of him, fight the LORD's battles (18:17).

  • vv27–31 "to those… in Hebron" — the towns of Judah that sheltered David and his men. Hebron is where the men of Judah… anointed David king over the house of Judah (2 Samuel 2:4).

chapters.title: The Death of Saul
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 31

Mount Gilboa

1The Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.

2The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and the Philistines struck down Jonathan, Abinadab and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.

3The battle pressed hard against Saul. The archers found him, and he was in great anguish because of the archers.

4Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through with it, or these uncircumcised will come and run me through and abuse me." But his armor-bearer would not, for he was greatly afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell on it.

5When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell on his sword and died with him.

6So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armor-bearer, and all his men, on that day together.

7When the men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley and on the other side of the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and fled, and the Philistines came and lived in them.

Jabesh-gilead

8And it came to pass the next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

9They cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and sent them throughout the land of the Philistines to carry the news to the house of their idols and to the people.

10They put his armor in the house of the Ashtaroth, and they fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.

11When the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,

12all the men of valor arose and went all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan. They came to Jabesh and burned them there.

13Then they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree at Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.

Notes

  • v2 "Jonathan, Abinadab and Malchi-shua" — Jonathan dies beside the father whose throne he gave up in words (23:17). The list of Saul's sons in 14:49 names Jonathan, Ishvi and Malchi-shua; a son of Saul who survives, Ish-bosheth, is made king by Abner (2 Samuel 2:8).

  • v3 "he was in great anguish because of the archers" — va-yachel, he writhed, was in anguish. The Greek has he was wounded in the belly.

  • v4 "Draw your sword and run me through with it" — Abimelech, dying at Thebez, said the same to his armor-bearer: Draw your sword and kill me, or they will say of me, "A woman killed him" (Judges 9:54). Abuse me, hit'allelu bi, the word of the Levite's secondary wife at Gibeah, whom the men abused all night (Judges 19:25). Saul's armor-bearer refuses; Abimelech's did not.

  • v4 "So Saul took the sword and fell on it" — an Amalekite will tell David a different story: I stood over him and killed him… and I took the crown that was on his head (2 Samuel 1:10).

  • v6 "on that day together" — Samuel's word at En-dor, tomorrow you and your sons will be with me (28:19), comes true on the next day.

  • v9 "They cut off his head" — as David cut off Goliath's (17:51). The Philistines carry the news to the house of their idols, as they once carried the ark into the house of Dagon (5:2).

  • v10 "the house of the Ashtaroth" — the goddesses Israel was told to put away from among them (7:3) and confessed to having served (12:10).

  • vv11–12 "the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead… went all night" — the town Saul saved in his first act as king (11:1–11). Its men march all night to rescue his body; he had reached their enemies' camp in the morning watch to rescue them (11:11).

  • v13 "under the tamarisk tree at Jabesh, and they fasted seven days" — Saul held court under the tamarisk tree on the height at Gibeah (22:6), and he is buried under one. Seven days is the time Jabesh once asked for while it waited for a rescuer (11:3). David later moves the bones of Saul and Jonathan from Jabesh (2 Samuel 21:12–14).
